title: GTA 6 pre-orders hit 9.69M as pre-load opens
description: GTA 6 pre-orders have reached an estimated 9.69 million, per Sensor Tower, as pre-load opens on PlayStation and Xbox ahead of launch next week.

body.text: GTA 6 pre-orders have made it the most pre-ordered game on both the PlayStation Store and the Microsoft Store, according to GamesIndustry.biz. Sensor Tower's tracker puts the global total at nearly 9.69 million, and with pre-loading now live, the focus is shifting from sales to whether launch day can handle the rush.
GTA 6 pre-orders: what the numbers show

Sensor Tower's GTA 6 sales tracker estimates about 9.69 million pre-orders worldwide, worth roughly $942 million in revenue. These are tracker estimates, not figures confirmed by Rockstar or Take-Two.

The growth in a single week is the striking part. On November 7, the same tracker showed close to eight million pre-orders and $751 million in revenue. That is a big jump in a short window, and it suggests demand is still climbing as release gets closer.
Take-Two says demand is beating its own forecast

Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick told GamesIndustry.biz that the company can't share the numbers, but pre-orders are far ahead of what it originally expected. Its earlier expectations, he said, matched the company's financial guidance.

Even so, Take-Two is keeping that guidance unchanged. Zelnick's reasoning, as reported, is that the release is only 10 days away and the company will know much more once the game is out. In its recent Q2 results, he also said Take-Two expects to deliver a historic year because of GTA 6.
GTA 6 pre-load: why it matters on launch day

Pre-loading has been available on PlayStation and Xbox since November 10. Both platforms recommend it to reduce the risk of crashes and delays when the game goes live. GamesIndustry.biz points to Hollow Knight: Silksong, which ran into launch-day trouble last year, as a recent example.
Experts consulted by the outlet are split on how much it will help:

items: GamesDiscoverCo newsletter author Simon Carless said having an extra nine days to spread out the bulk of the data is vital. A Day 1 patch or extra download may still arrive, but it should be very incremental.

Investor and strategic advisor Joost van Dreunen warned that the bottleneck could still hit on launch day, when tens of millions of day-of buyers, rather than a few hundred thousand, will be downloading.

body.text: In practice, pre-loading handles the biggest chunk of the data. It may not cover late buyers or any patch that lands at the last minute.

Keep an eye on the Sensor Tower tracker, which should show whether pre-orders keep rising right up to release. Also watch for any Day 1 patch announcement and how the PlayStation and Xbox networks cope when day-of buyers start downloading. If you own a console, pre-load now so you aren't waiting in that queue. Take-Two's next update after launch should give a clearer picture of how the numbers hold up.

sources.title: GTA 6 becomes most pre-ordered game on PlayStation and Xbox storefronts
